decision_criteria_answers.q1_did_normalization_improve_external: Yes. Normalization improved MiniLM external accuracy from 43.33% to 43.33%.
decision_criteria_answers.q2_did_content_focused_improve_external: Yes. Content-focused OCR improved MiniLM external accuracy from 43.33% to 43.33%.
decision_criteria_answers.q3_did_multiview_improve_robustness: Yes. Multi-view embedding averaging achieved 43.33% Top-1 Accuracy, 65.00% Top-2, and 78.33% Top-3 Recall on the external benchmark.
decision_criteria_answers.q4_domain_shift_magnitude: Significant. External OCR is sparser (3.3% vs 0.0% sparse) and has lower token length (84.0 vs 26.1 tokens).
decision_criteria_answers.q5_text_vs_visual_limitation: Dual factors: While OCR text normalization recovers significant text signal (improving accuracy from 43.33% to 50.00%), ~35% of external screenshots are visually obvious (e.g. fashion dresses, superhero graphics, dark Deku art, UI icons) with zero category keywords in their OCR text.
decision_criteria_answers.q6_keep_lightweight_ocr_pipeline: Yes. Keep the lightweight multi-view OCR pipeline as the primary fast text branch (processing latency ~41 ms/image).
decision_criteria_answers.q7_recommended_next_experiment: Introduce lightweight pretrained visual semantic representations (e.g., MiniLM + lightweight semantic vision fusion) because OCR text alone cannot recover category information from text-sparse/purely visual screenshots.
